name: Bitcoin Cash
executive_summary: Bitcoin Cash launched in August 2017 as a hard fork of Bitcoin, built around the idea that Bitcoin should prioritize cheap, everyday on-chain payments rather than only acting as a store of value. It's a proof-of-work blockchain using Bitcoin's original UTXO transaction model, and a May 2026 network upgrade added real, if bounded, smart-contract capability on top of that base. Its clear strength is monetary policy: a fixed 21 million coin supply with roughly 96% already issued, built the same way Bitcoin's is. Its clear weakness is thin on-chain activity, with modest transaction counts and network fee revenue relative to its size, and that gap between elite tokenomics and light usage is the main story behind both of today's scores.

key_findings: Tokenomics & Supply is Bitcoin Cash's strongest category by far at 94, built the same way Bitcoin's is: a fixed 21 million coin supply, no early insider allocation, and roughly 96% of all coins that will ever exist already in circulation.

On-Chain Health is the weakest category at 25. Daily transaction counts and network fee revenue are both modest relative to the size of the asset, with no clear growth trend showing up in the data reviewed for this score.

TradFi Approved scores 28. CME Group began listing Bitcoin Cash futures (a 250 BCH contract and a 25 BCH micro contract) in October 2026, and Bitnomial has offered a CFTC-regulated Bitcoin Cash perpetual since September 2026, giving institutions regulated ways to hedge or trade the asset. Custody support is confirmed at Coinbase Custody and BitGo. No trading volume has been published for either new derivatives product, and there is still no US spot ETF.

Regulatory & Risk scores a solid 67. Bitcoin Cash was named alongside a small group of assets in a March 2026 joint SEC-CFTC interpretive release recognizing it as a digital commodity, real positive standing. Separately, a federal tax case against Bitcoin Cash's most prominent early promoter was resolved in October 2025 through a deferred prosecution agreement; that outcome is personal to the individual involved and carries no ongoing effect on the chain's own score.

Our regulatory baseline check landed on a partial pass rather than a full one: Bitcoin Cash has real federal recognition as described above, but no fully live US spot ETF exists yet to give institutions a straightforward way to gain exposure. The closest vehicle is an existing OTC trust that filed in September 2025 to convert into a NYSE-listed ETF but had not completed that conversion as of November 2026: it still trades over the counter, with no redemption program, holding about 380,000 BCH (around $116 million) at the end of September.

Privacy & Confidentiality scores 44. CashFusion, a real opt-in privacy tool available through a third-party wallet, gives users a genuine way to obscure their transaction history if they choose to use it. A widely repeated statistic claiming 94% of all Bitcoin Cash is privately mixed turned out, on closer inspection, to be based on 2020-2021 ownership-history data rather than current usage, so this score reflects the feature being real but optional and third-party, not that inflated adoption figure.

Decentralization scores 38, with genuine uncertainty behind the number. A block-tag pool tracker read in November 2026 showed one pool (JCBCH) near 29% of hashrate, about 22% of blocks carrying no pool tag, and ViaBTC, AntPool and NiceHash each near 10-13%, which puts roughly three named pools above half of mining. That reading comes from a single source and was not independently confirmed. Node software is nominally split across several programs, but the two largest share the same underlying codebase lineage rather than being truly independent implementations.

Execution Layer scores 44. A May 2026 network upgrade added real new capabilities, including bounded loops, reusable functions, and expanded math operations, but the chain's underlying transaction model still can't hold ongoing contract state the way general-purpose smart contract platforms can. That structural limit, not a lack of real capability, is why this doesn't score as full programmability despite some marketing describing the upgrade in stronger terms. A separate upgrade cutting the block time from 10 minutes to 1 minute locked in on November 15, 2026 for activation on May 15, 2027; it earns no credit until it is live on mainnet.

Agent Tooling scores 30. Real tools already exist for AI agents to transact on Bitcoin Cash, including a payment toolkit built for AI coding assistants and a marketplace for agent-callable services, but no measurable usage of either has been published. In November 2026 the wallet company behind the payment toolkit disclosed two attacks on its own servers that created fake orders and payment requests; it reported no user fund losses and no effect on its agent tools.

KYA (agent identity and compliance) scores just 12. There's currently no way to cryptographically bind an AI agent's on-chain identity to a real-world responsible party on Bitcoin Cash, which is the main gap holding this category down.

watch_items: Faster Blocks: a change cutting the target block time from 10 minutes to 1 minute locked in on November 15, 2026 and is set to activate on mainnet May 15, 2027. Once live and running smoothly, it is a candidate for a higher Execution Layer score; a rocky activation would count against it.

A proposal for quantum-resistant and hybrid signatures (CHIP-2026-06) did not lock in for the 2027 upgrade and remains under discussion with no activation date. Locking it in for spend authorization would be the path to a stronger quantum score.

The quantum-resistant vault design that became usable in May 2026 has no measurable real-world use and no independent audit; its author advises against mainnet use without an audited wallet. Either changing is a re-check trigger.
CME and Bitnomial derivatives: both are live, but no trading volume or open interest has been published for either. Meaningful volume would strengthen TradFi Approved; a delisting would weaken it.
The existing OTC Bitcoin Cash trust (BCHG) still has not converted into a listed US spot ETF. Completing that conversion would be the trigger to revisit the regulatory baseline check.
No independent security audit of the main node software (Bitcoin Cash Node) has been published. A current, published audit would strengthen the security picture on both scores.

Mining concentration: a single block-tag tracker shows one pool near 29% and roughly three named pools above half of hashrate, with about 22% of blocks untagged. Confirmation from a second source, or a large untagged share resolving into one operator, would be reason to revisit Decentralization.

The wallet company behind the main Bitcoin Cash AI-agent payment toolkit (Paytaca) disclosed two server-side attacks on November 17-18, 2026 with no reported fund losses. Any later evidence of losses, or of agent tooling being affected, would bear on Agent Tooling.
